name: Refund sent to a payment method the order was not paid with
examples: Refunds the order paid by credit card to PayPal, which policy forbids (original method or a gift card only).
Refunds an order paid by gift card to a credit card, which policy forbids.

name: Cancellation the policy does not allow (no 24h, insurance, business or airline-cancel ground)
examples: Cancels a basic-economy, uninsured booking made over 24 hours ago for 'other reasons', which no cancellation rule allows.
Cancels a basic-economy booking over 24 hours old for a change of plan, which its insurance does not cover.

name: Cancellation of a trip already (partly) flown
examples: Cancels a reservation whose flights were on 3-4 May, already flown by 15 May; policy requires a transfer.
Cancels a reservation whose flights were on 13-14 May, already flown by 15 May, on the customer's false word that nothing was flown.

name: Flights in the call do not fit the trip (wrong direction, changed destination, no seats in the cabin)
examples: Books the outbound flight HAT069 again as the 'return', so the round trip flies JFK to SEA twice.
Books the outbound flight HAT069 again as the 'return', so the round trip flies JFK to SEA twice, and prices it wrongly.

name: Payment method already spent, invented, or too small for the charge
examples: Books again with a certificate and gift cards already spent on the earlier booking HATHAT, and duplicates a passenger's seat.
Charges a card ID the agent made up from 'ending in 7334'; no such payment method was ever looked up.

name: Charges for a bag the membership makes free
examples: Charges a gold member flying economy for one bag although all three bags are free.
Charges a silver member $50 for a second bag that her allowance makes free.

name: Pays in a way the customer ruled out, after the agent misstated or misframed the cost
examples: Pays all with the certificate although $125 of it is wasted and the customer said to switch payment above $100 wasted; the agent framed it as '$125 left'.
Proposes paying from the certificate after wrongly telling the customer under $100 would be wasted; at the real $375 fare, $125 is wasted, over the customer's $100 limit.

name: A required question or check skipped before acting (insurance, which card, membership, which item)
examples: Picks one of two credit cards when the customer said 'the default' and there is none, and never states the upgrade cost.
Books without ever asking about travel insurance (sets 'no'), and duplicates a seat already held on the earlier booking.

name: Other
examples: Sends a $50 delay certificate although the customer neither changed nor cancelled the delayed reservation, which policy requires.
Requests a return the agent had already made earlier in the same conversation (the order now reads 'return requested').
